definitions.gloss: peak, summit, top of a mountain
definitions.explanation: The highest point of a mountain or elevation. A literary alternative to {山頂|さんちょう} or {頂上|ちょうじょう}.
The highest point or most intense moment of something — power, popularity, emotion, or any state. More commonly used than the literal mountain sense.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}の{絶頂|ぜっちょう}に{立|た}つ。
examples.english: Stand on the summit of the mountain.

examples.japanese: {登山家|とざんか}たちは{吹雪|ふぶき}の{中|なか}、{絶頂|ぜっちょう}を{目指|めざ}した。
examples.english: The mountaineers pressed toward the summit in the blizzard.

examples.japanese: {険|けわ}しい{岩場|いわば}を{越|こ}えて、ついに{絶頂|ぜっちょう}にたどり{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: After crossing steep rocky terrain, they finally reached the summit.

examples.japanese: {人気|にんき}{絶頂|ぜっちょう}のアイドルだ。
examples.english: An idol at the height of popularity.

examples.japanese: {幸福|こうふく}の{絶頂|ぜっちょう}にいる{気分|きぶん}だった。
examples.english: I felt like I was at the peak of happiness.

examples.japanese: ローマ{帝国|ていこく}は2{世紀|せいき}に{権力|けんりょく}の{絶頂|ぜっちょう}を{迎|むか}えた。
examples.english: The Roman Empire reached the zenith of its power in the 2nd century.

notes:
USAGE:
The figurative sense (peak, zenith) is more common than the literal mountain summit sense. Often used in the pattern ○○の{絶頂|ぜっちょう} or ○○{絶頂|ぜっちょう} (at the peak of ○○).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {頂上|ちょうじょう}: summit, top (more common for mountains)
- {山頂|さんちょう}: mountain summit (specific to mountains)
- {最高潮|さいこうちょう}: climax, high point (of excitement or events)
- {全盛期|ぜんせいき}: heyday, golden age (focuses on the period)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人気|にんき}{絶頂|ぜっちょう}: at the height of popularity
- {幸福|こうふく}の{絶頂|ぜっちょう}: peak of happiness
- {権力|けんりょく}の{絶頂|ぜっちょう}: zenith of power
- {絶頂期|ぜっちょうき}: peak period
